Anselm of Canterbury on faith

Anselm of Canterbury (c. 1033–1109) approaches faith within Scholasticism. He formulated an ontological argument and theories of atonement while defending rational reflection on doctrine. Systematically, the teaching links faith, reason, God into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets faith most directly—useful for searches such as “anselm of canterbury quotes on faith.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Anselm of Canterbury thinker page for biography and to the faith theme for other voices on the same question.
